text:
Maya Patel: hey team, new hire here 👋 followed the k8s onboarding but I only see dev/prod contexts, no staging. mac M1.

DevEx Bot: welcome Maya! quick checks: `echo $KUBECONFIG` and `kubectl config get-contexts -o name`. also did you run the cloud provider update step?

Maya Patel: `kubectl config get-contexts -o name` -> redwood-dev, redwood-prod
`echo $KUBECONFIG` -> /Users/maya/.kube/config:/Users/maya/.kube/config-aws

Sam Kim: looks like `config-aws` contains staging. try `KUBECONFIG=/Users/maya/.kube/config-aws kubectl config get-contexts -o name`. If it shows `redwood-staging-us-west-2` merge with `kubectl config view --flatten > ~/.kube/merged-config` then `export KUBECONFIG=~/.kube/merged-config`.

Maya Patel: that showed the staging context. ran `aws sso login` and `aws eks update-kubeconfig` too. when I switch to staging and run `kubectl get pods -n staging` I get Forbidden.

Sam Kim: that's RBAC — I can apply a RoleBinding giving view on staging. DM me your company email.

Maya Patel: maya.patel@redwood.example.com

Sam Kim: applied `rb-maya-staging-view` bound to group `redwood-engineers`. try `kubectl auth can-i list pods -n staging` then `kubectl get pods -n staging`.

Maya Patel: `kubectl auth can-i list pods -n staging` -> yes. pods show up now. thanks! I'll add a note to the onboarding doc about KUBECONFIG ordering and SSO steps.
